equations.statement: For an angle BOA of one degree, the ratio of BM to MA is very nearly 114.589, so BM contains MA more than 114 times.

symbols.meaning: segment from M to A along OA

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Ratios of Continuously Increasing or Decreasing Quantities
equations.statement: The angle at the centre O subtended by the arc AB is denoted theta.

symbols.meaning: the angle BOA at the centre O

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Notion of Infinitely Small Quantities
equations.statement: Squaring a sum a + h expands to a^2 + 2ah + h^2, so increasing a by h increases a^2 by 2ah + h^2.

symbols.meaning: a magnitude (number) that is increased by h

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Notion of Infinitely Small Quantities
equations.statement: As 1 contains h, so many times, h contains h^2; the four quantities 1, h, h, h^2 are in proportion.

symbols.meaning: a small quantity (the increment), taken as a magnitude less than the unit

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On Functions
equations.statement: An illustrative function: φx is defined as x plus x squared, so φ is the direction to add x to its square.

symbols.meaning: the abbreviated direction to perform the operation (here: add x to its square); not a number multiplying x
the variable on which the function acts

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Infinite Series
equations.name: Taylor's theorem (series expansion)
equations.statement: A function of x + h can generally be expanded as an infinite series in whole, positive powers of h, with the constant term phi x.

symbols.meaning: coefficient of h in the expansion
coefficient of h^2 in the expansion
coefficient of h^3 in the expansion

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Infinite Series
equations.statement: The increment of phi x is the difference between phi(x + h) and phi x, negative when phi(x + h) is less than phi x.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Infinite Series
equations.statement: The increment of phi x is negative exactly when phi(x + h) is less than phi x.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Infinite Series
equations.statement: For x less than unity, the infinite geometric series 1 + x + x^2 + ... can be brought as near as we please to 1/(1 - x), so the series is said to equal it.

symbols.meaning: a number supposed less than unity

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Convergent and Divergent Series
equations.statement: The series a + b + c + d + ... can be rewritten as a times a series whose terms are successive ratios of the original terms.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Convergent and Divergent Series
equations.statement: The same rewriting holds when the series is taken from any term k onward: the tail sum equals k times a series of successive ratios.

symbols.meaning: the term of the series from which the rewriting starts

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Convergent and Divergent Series
equations.statement: The successive ratios of the terms are assumed to decrease, so each ratio is greater than the next.

symbols.meaning: the term from which the series is taken

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: The power (x + h)^n is developed in ascending powers of the increment h, with the coefficients of h, h^2/2 and h^3/(2·3) given.

symbols.meaning: a small increment added to x

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: The logarithm of x + h is developed in powers of the increment h.

symbols.meaning: a small increment added to x

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.latex: \cos(x + h) = \cos x - \sin x\, h - \cos x\, \frac{h^{2}}{2} + \sin x\, \frac{h^{3}}{2·3}
equations.statement: The cosine of x + h is developed in powers of h; the terms are positive and negative in pairs.

symbols.meaning: a small increment added to x

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.name: Taylor's theorem
equations.statement: A function phi(x + h) is expanded as a series in powers of h whose coefficients are the successive derived functions of phi at x, divided by factorials.

symbols.meaning: the function (general symbol for a function)
a small increment added to x
the first derived function (derivative) of phi
the second derived function of phi
the third derived function of phi

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: When phi x = x^n, its first derived function is n x^(n-1).

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: When phi x = x^n, its second derived function is n(n - 1) x^(n-2).

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: When phi x = sin x, its first derived function is cos x.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: When phi x = sin x, its second derived function is minus sin x.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: When phi x = a^x, its first derived function is k a^x, where k is the natural logarithm of a.

symbols.meaning: the natural (Naperian or hyperbolic) logarithm of a

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: The first derived function of a^x, evaluated at x + h, is k a^(x+h), developed in powers of h.

symbols.meaning: a small increment added to x

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: The reciprocal 1/(x + h) is developed in powers of h, found by common division.

symbols.meaning: a small increment added to x

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Taylor's Theorem. Derived Functions
equations.statement: The second derived function of log x, evaluated at x + h, equals minus one over (x + h) squared.

symbols.meaning: a small increment added to x

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Differential Coefficients
equations.statement: The function of x+h, expanded in powers of the increment h, has as its coefficients the function, its first, second and third differential coefficients divided by the factorials 1, 2, 2·3 (the displayed right-hand side; the chapter does not write the left-hand side).

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Differential Coefficients
equations.statement: The increment of the function produced by changing x into x+h is the series in h whose first term is φ'x·h. Note: the chapter prints a stray letter x after h²/2 in this line; this is recorded as printed and flagged as a probable typesetting error in the book.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Differential Coefficients
equations.latex: \frac{\emph{increment of } \phi x}{\emph{increment of } x} = \phi' x + \phi'' x\, \frac{h}{2} x + \phi''' x\, \frac{h^{2}}{2·3} + \etc.
equations.statement: The ratio of the increment of the function to the increment of its variable equals φ'x plus a series in h that vanishes as h diminishes. Note: the chapter prints a stray letter x after h/2 in this line; recorded as printed and flagged as a probable typesetting error in the book.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Differential Coefficients
equations.statement: The part of the ratio other than its first term φ'x is written as h times a series; this is an expression for that remainder (no equality sign in the chapter).

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Differential Coefficients
equations.statement: The ratio of the term kh^n to the tail lh^(n+1)+mh^(n+2)+… is the same as the ratio of k to lh+mh²+…; a proportion used to show the tail can be made a small part of the term kh^n.

symbols.meaning: a given quantity independent of h
the power index of the term
coefficient of the next power of h
coefficient of the following power of h

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Notation of the Differential Calculus
equations.statement: The increment of x squared, found by expanding (x + dx)^2, equals 2x dx plus the square of dx.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Notation of the Differential Calculus
equations.statement: Dividing the increment of x^2 by the increment of x gives 2x plus dx, which tends to 2x as dx diminishes.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Notation of the Differential Calculus
equations.statement: The ratio of the increment of x^2 to the increment of x is, in the limit, 2x; in the first explanation this equation is strictly true.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Notation of the Differential Calculus
equations.statement: For y = x^2 the ratio of the increment of y to the increment of x equals 2x plus dx.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Notation of the Differential Calculus
equations.statement: The ratio of the increment of y to the increment of x, with dx made zero, is 2x; this is the limit of the ratio, not a ratio of two actual quantities.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Notation of the Differential Calculus
equations.statement: The increment of y for y = x^2 is 2x dx plus the square of dx; the (dx)^2 term affects dy but not the limit of dy/dx.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Algebraical Geometry
equations.statement: The ordinate y of a moving point P is always equal to the square of its abscissa x, so P traces a parabola (the book's example of a curve given by a function).

symbols.meaning: ordinate PM of the point P (distance measured parallel to OB, the axis of y)
abscissa OM of the point P (distance measured along OA, the axis of x)

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.name: equation of the circle
equations.statement: A point whose co-ordinates are x and y lies on a circle of radius r centred at the origin O exactly when x squared plus y squared equals r squared.

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate OM of the point P (abscissa)
co-ordinate MP of the point P (ordinate)

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The straight line EF, cutting the axes at distances a and b from O, satisfies ay + bx = ab for every one of its points, with the signs of x and y taken in the stated directions.

symbols.meaning: length OE, where the line EF cuts the axis of x
length OF, where the line EF cuts the axis of y

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: For a point P' on EF produced, with x taken as the signed co-ordinate, the relation is ay - bx = ab, which is the earlier equation with the sign of x changed.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: For a point P'' on FE produced, the relation is bx - ay = ab, which is the earlier equation with the sign of y changed.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: Substituting the value of y from the line equation into the circle equation gives this equation in x alone.

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate OM of the intersection point P

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The abscissas x of the points where the line meets the circle are the roots of this quadratic equation in x.

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate OM of the intersection point

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The ordinates y of the points where the line meets the circle are the roots of this quadratic equation in y.

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate MP of the intersection point

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The abscissas of the two intersection points of the line and the circle, taking the upper or the lower sign throughout.

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate OM of the intersection point

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The ordinates of the two intersection points of the line and the circle, with the sign of the root taken opposite to that in the formula for x.

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate MP of the intersection point

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The line meets the circle in two points exactly when r is greater than the perpendicular from O to EF, whose length is ab over the square root of a squared plus b squared.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The two intersection points coincide and the straight line EF is a tangent to the circle.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The values of x and y are impossible and the straight line does not meet the circle.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: Squaring a negative value of x gives the same result as squaring the positive value, so the left branch of the curve mirrors the right.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The length OE, measured along the axis of x, is called a and is the intercept of the straight line EF on that axis.

symbols.meaning: length OE, intercept of the line EF on the axis of x

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: On the Connexion of the Signs of Algebraical and the Directions of Geometrical Magnitudes
equations.statement: The length OF, measured along the axis of y, is called b and is the intercept of the straight line EF on that axis.

symbols.meaning: length OF, intercept of the line EF on the axis of y

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Drawing of a Tangent to a Curve
equations.statement: When x increases by dx, the point on the curve has co-ordinates x + dx and y + dy, and the curve relation still holds for them.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Drawing of a Tangent to a Curve
equations.statement: When P' is placed on the other side of P, at co-ordinates x - dx and y - dy, the curve relation holds for those co-ordinates.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Drawing of a Tangent to a Curve
equations.statement: Subtracting the backward relation from y = x^2 gives the increment of y for the backward step.

symbols.meaning: increment of y for the backward step

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Drawing of a Tangent to a Curve
equations.statement: For the backward step, the ratio of the increment of y to the increment of x equals 2x minus dx, which approaches 2x as dx diminishes.

symbols.meaning: ratio of the increment of y to the increment of x for the backward step

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Drawing of a Tangent to a Curve
equations.statement: The ordinate y is some function of the abscissa x, written as phi x.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Drawing of a Tangent to a Curve
equations.statement: For the curve whose ordinates are the Naperian logarithms of the abscissae, y equals the natural logarithm of x.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Drawing of a Tangent to a Curve
equations.statement: The incremented ordinate of the logarithmic curve, expanded in powers of dx, is log x plus dx/x minus dx^2/(2x^2), with further terms omitted (etc.).

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Rational Explanation of the Language of Leibnitz
equations.statement: The curve PP' is the graph of y equal to a given function of x, so PM is found by substituting OM into that function.

symbols.meaning: ordinate PM of a point on the curve
the given function of x whose graph is the curve

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Rational Explanation of the Language of Leibnitz
equations.statement: The increment of x, taken as the segment MM', is written dx; it may be supposed as small as we please.

symbols.meaning: the increment of OM from M to M'

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Rational Explanation of the Language of Leibnitz
equations.statement: The increment P'Q of the ordinate equals a series in powers of dx, whose first term is phi'(x) dx, with higher derivatives divided by factorials.

symbols.meaning: increment of the ordinate y, equal to dy = phi(x + dx) - phi(x)
first differential coefficient of phi at x
second differential coefficient of phi at x
third differential coefficient of phi at x

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Rational Explanation of the Language of Leibnitz
equations.statement: The chord PP' equals dx times the square root of one plus the square of dy over dx.

symbols.meaning: chord joining P and P' on the curve

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Rational Explanation of the Language of Leibnitz
equations.statement: The tangent of the angle VPQ times PQ gives VQ, so the first term of the series is the segment VQ along the tangent.

symbols.meaning: angle between the tangent PV and the line PQ at P
segment of the tangent from V to Q

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: Orders of Infinity
equations.statement: The increment QP' along the curve, to the first two orders in dx, is the first derivative of phi at x times dx plus the second derivative times half (dx) squared, with further terms omitted.

symbols.meaning: first differential coefficient (first derivative) of phi at x
second differential coefficient (second derivative) of phi at x
the small increment PQ of the variable x, put in place of h
the segment QP' of the curve in Fig. 4, shown in the chapter as the expansion itself (the chapter gives the expression without an explicit equals sign)

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.name: Pythagorean theorem
equations.statement: The squares of the two axial segments OA and OB add up to the square of the length of the sliding line AB.

symbols.meaning: OA, the length of the segment from O to A on one axis
OB, the length of the segment from O to B on the other axis
AB, the given fixed length of the sliding line

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: In the displaced position the line still has length l, with its ends at a + da and b - db along the axes.

symbols.meaning: AA', the increment of OA when the line moves
BB', the decrement of OB when the line moves
AB, the fixed length of the line

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Subtracting the first length equation from the displaced one gives a relation between the increments da and db.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: The ratio of the increment db to the increment da equals (2a + da)/(2b - db); this is equation (1).

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Every point (x, y) of the line AB satisfies this equation in the coordinate axes; this is equation (2).

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate of a point measured along the axis OC (OM for P')
co-ordinate of a point measured parallel to OC (MP for P)

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: The line of the displaced position, which cuts off a + da and b - db from the axes, has this equation; this is equation (3).

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.latex: y\, da - x\, db = b\, da - a\, db - da\, db\Add{.}
equations.statement: Subtracting equation (2) from equation (3) gives this relation for the point P' of intersection; this is equation (4).

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate of P' parallel to OC

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.latex: y - x\, \frac{2a + da}{2b - db} = b - a\, \frac{2a + da}{2b - db} - db\Add{.}
equations.statement: Dividing equation (4) by da and substituting db/da from equation (1) gives this relation; this is equation (5).

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate of P' parallel to OC

equations.sympy: Eq(y - x*(2*a + da)/(2*b - db), b - a*(2*a + da)/(2*b - db) - db)

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Equation (5) with da and db diminished without limit gives this line through the limit point P; the same line in cleared form is equation (6).

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate of the limit point P along OC
co-ordinate of the limit point P parallel to OC

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Cleared of fractions, the limit of the intersections satisfies this equation; this is equation (6).

symbols.meaning: co-ordinate of the limit point P along OC
co-ordinate of the limit point P parallel to OC

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Solving equations (6) and (2) gives the co-ordinate x of the limit point P as a^3 over l^2.

symbols.meaning: OM, co-ordinate of the limit point P along OC

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Solving equations (6) and (2) gives the co-ordinate y of the limit point P as b^3 over l^2.

symbols.meaning: MP, co-ordinate of the limit point P parallel to OC

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: By similar triangles the distance BP from B to the limit point equals a^2 over l.

symbols.meaning: distance from B to the limit point P

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Similarly, the distance PA from A to the limit point equals b^2 over l.

symbols.meaning: distance from A to the limit point P

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Since OA is a mean proportional between AQ and AB (OQ perpendicular to BA), AQ equals a^2 over l.

symbols.meaning: distance from A to the foot Q of the perpendicular from O to AB

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: Similarly, BQ equals b^2 over l, the distance from B to the foot Q.

symbols.meaning: distance from B to the foot Q of the perpendicular from O to AB

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: A Geometrical Illustration: Limit of the Intersections of Two Coinciding Straight Lines
equations.statement: The limit point P lies as far from B as Q lies from A, so the limit of the intersections is found by this construction.

symbols.meaning: distance from B to the limit point P
distance from A to the foot Q

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Same Problem Solved by the Principles of Leibnitz
equations.statement: The length BP is denoted q.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Same Problem Solved by the Principles of Leibnitz
equations.statement: The infinitely small increment Aa is denoted dp.

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Same Problem Solved by the Principles of Leibnitz
equations.latex: Aa : A'a :: OA : OB :: a : b
equations.statement: Corresponding sides of the small triangles at A are in the same ratio as the radii OA and OB.

symbols.meaning: point A on the line AB

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Same Problem Solved by the Principles of Leibnitz
equations.latex: Bb : B'b :: OA : OB :: a : b
equations.statement: The small arcs at B are in the same proportion as the radii, so this ratio matches the one at A.

symbols.meaning: point B on the line AB

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Same Problem Solved by the Principles of Leibnitz
equations.statement: The composed proportion obtained from the two proportions above, with Aa equal to B'b, relates the arc Bb to A'a.

symbols.meaning: distance from B to the point P

equations.edition: Open Court Publishing Company, Chicago, new ed., 1899
equations.location: The Same Problem Solved by the Principles of Leibnitz
equations.statement: After cancelling the common factor, the segments BP and Pa stand in the same proportion as a² + b² and b².
